# Dashboard Starter

Copy this file to
`assignments/assignment07-dashboard/submission/dashboard.qmd` before editing.
Keep this original starter unchanged so you can compare your adaptation with it.

## Where this fits

This is the **required core artifact** for Assignment 7. The Shiny exemplar
shown in class is a demonstration only; adapt this Quarto file instead.

## Goal

This starter shows how to turn the Week 7 descriptive summary into a dashboard-style KT product. It uses one editable control value, one visualization, one table, one interpretation, and one caution — the 1-1-1-1-1 rule made concrete.

## Audience Question

Audience: a public-health analyst preparing a short briefing on descriptive BMI patterns in the classroom NHANES equity dataset.

Question: among adults age 20-80, how does mean BMI vary across NHANES cycles for one selected income group?

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)  # AI-EDIT(2026-06-23): tidyverse-default — consolidated core library() calls into library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Control

In a Shiny app, this would become a dropdown. In this static starter, change the value of `selected_income` and render again.

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
selected_income <- "Middle Income"

if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): MIT-081 — needs review -->
For example, change the line to `selected_income <- "Middle Income"` — the other valid value in the classroom dataset is `"High Income (>3.5)"`. Copy the value exactly, including the quotes and any parentheses.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(dashboard_summary)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
# Figure (caption revised for A7; text only)
# AI prompt (condensed from Claude chat): "Rewrite this ggplot2 caption for program managers who
#   will see the figure in slides. The plot shows mean_bmi (numeric) by Cycle (character, 11 values
#   from 1999-2000 to 2021-2023, no 2019-2020) for one IncomeGroup ('Low Income (<1.3)', 'Middle
#   Income' or 'High Income (>3.5)'), adults with Age 20-80 and BMI and Cycle present. Explain the
#   statistic, NHANES cycle, income cut-offs, missing cycle and zoomed y-axis, and add one
#   non-causal limitation. One sentence per line, true for every income group."
# Verified: count(IncomeGroup, Cycle) for adults 20-80 with BMI, IncomeGroup and Cycle present
#   gives 11 cycles per group, a minimum n of 1,089 and no 2019-2020 cycle; exclusions match
#   filter() in the Summary chunk; render shows all six caption lines in full and a y-axis that
#   does not start at 0; no causal or population wording.
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2f6f73") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = "#2f6f73") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Mean BMI for", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = paste(
      "Each point is the mean BMI (kg/m²) of more than 1,000 adults in one survey wave (NHANES cycle).",
      "Income groups use the family income-to-poverty ratio, with cut-offs at 1.3 and 3.5.",
      "The dataset has no 2019-2020 cycle, and the y-axis does not start at 0.",
      "Excludes ages outside 20-80 and records missing BMI, income group or cycle.",
      "This unweighted, descriptive summary does not give national estimates",
      "or show that income causes differences in BMI.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Interpretation

For the selected income group, the table and figure describe the mean BMI pattern across available NHANES cycles in the prepared classroom dataset. The dashboard should help the audience ask better questions about pattern, timing, and context rather than treat the line as a causal explanation.

## Limitation

This starter is unweighted and descriptive. It does not account for NHANES survey design, does not estimate national prevalence, and should not be used to make causal claims about income and BMI.

## Testing

Before submitting a dashboard-style product:

1. Render this page from the repository root.
2. Change `selected_income` to another value from `available_income_groups`.
3. Render again and check that the table, title, and plot all update.
4. Verify that the caption still names the dataset, exclusions, and limitation.
5. Record any warning or error in your testing log.

From the repository root, render the submitted copy with:

```bash
quarto render assignments/assignment07-dashboard/submission/dashboard.qmd
```

HTML is the expected output for this dashboard — you do not need a PDF. If the render log warns about a missing TeX installation or a PDF problem, you can ignore it as long as the `.html` file was created. <!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-22): REVIEW-row190 / MIT-080 — added cross-ref so the brief HTML/PDF reminder reads as intentional reinforcement of the fuller routine on dash05, not accidental duplication -->
The Week 8 course page walks through the full six-step test routine.

## Privacy-Safe Publishing

- Use aggregate summaries, not row-level records.
- Avoid small-cell interpretations when `n` is low.
- State that outputs are descriptive and unweighted.
- Keep cached classroom data separate from any raw NHANES retrieval workflow.
- Do not upload row-level data to external AI tools.
